problem:
Title: Interval containing Prime Number of forms 4n - 1, 4n + 1, 6n - 1, 6n + 1

Let $n \in \Z$ be an [[Definition:Integer|integer]] such that $n \ge 118$.

Then between $n$ and $\dfrac {4 n} 3$ there exists at least one [[Definition:Prime Number|prime number]] of each of the forms:
:$4 m - 1, 4 m + 1, 6 m - 1, 6 m + 1$

0052 | So it can be seen that:

0066 | and so the conditions of the result are fulfilled for $118$.

0068 | But then note we have:
0069 | 
0070 | :$\dfrac {4 \times 117} 3 = 156$
0071 | 
0072 | and so the [[Definition:Prime Number|primes]] between $117$ and $157$ are the same ones as between $118$ and $157$, excluding $157$ itself.
0073 | 
0074 | Thus the conditions also hold for $117$.
0075 | 
0076 | It is puzzling as to why the condition $n \ge 118$ has been applied to the initial statement.
